description: Split a Canvas Spaces bundle by what each space IS — the value of a parameter on its attached object (default `identifyingType`). Matching spaces leave on the first output, the rest on the second.
instructions:
Answers the question a flow could not previously ask: WHICH of these spaces is a road, and which is a plot.

A Canvas bundle is geometry — polygons and nothing else — so until now every space in it looked alike. This node reads the parametric object ATTACHED to each space and keeps the ones whose named parameter equals Type.

WIRING: Canvas → Spaces → Filter by Type. Two geometry outputs: out-0 MATCHING, out-1 REST. Wire the one you want onward; leaving the other unwired is normal (use it to draw the complement, or to check nothing was missed).

PARAMETERS
• TYPE — the value to match, compared case-insensitively after trimming ("Road" matches "road"). Blank matches nothing rather than everything: a half-typed filter should produce no plots, not all of them.
• PARAMETER KEY — which parameter carries the classification. Defaults to `identifyingType`, the read-only tag plot.json and road.json declare. Point it at another key to slice by something else — the same Spaces bundle can be filtered by `color`, or by any select the attached object exposes.

WHAT IT MATCHES AGAINST is the attached object's parameters with the instance's edits on top, so a space answers with its default classification even if that parameter was added to the object AFTER the object was placed. A space with NO attached object matches nothing and always lands in Rest.

MATCHING BY TAG, NOT BY OBJECT ID, is deliberate. An id (`road-with-math`) breaks the moment the object is renamed and cannot express "these three different objects are all roads". A tag is stable and shared.

BOTH HALVES ARE ALSO VALUES. `val-matching` / `val-rest` carry the same polygons as a GROUPED FLAT matrix — one row per vertex, `[x, y, groupIndex]`, anchor-relative metres — which is how geometry reaches a Math Engine, since only a value wire can. Feed either into an expression and `inpoly` reads the group column back as one ring per space. `val-matchCount` / `val-restCount` are the counts.

IDENTITY IS RESOLVED BY POSITION IN THE CANVAS BUNDLE, so wire this DIRECTLY to a Canvas output. An op in between (Inset, Transform, Merge …) rebuilds the polygons and their correspondence to the canvas is lost — filter FIRST, then operate on the half you kept.

It produces no geometry of its own and commits nothing: it is a selector, so it is preview / Flow-Live only and never appears as a recipe op.
